specific_rules: Structural steel shall conform to requirements listed on the Structural General Notes.
Steel angles and plates to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Channels to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Steel W shapes (I sections) and tees to NBN EN 10025 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Hollow structural sections to NBN EN 10210 Grade S355JR unless otherwise noted.
Steel used on the project is to be Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as defined by NBN EN 1090-2 unless noted otherwise on the A/E drawings.
Steel sections for miscellaneous metal fabrications to EN 10025.
Steel hollow sections for miscellaneous metal fabrications to EN 10210.

materials.category: Cold-Formed / Sheet Steel for Decking and Fabrications
specific_rules: Steel deck units and sheet accessories to be produced from galvanized steel sheet conforming to NBN EN 10346 and NBN EN 10143, Grade of steel S350 unless indicated or agreed otherwise.
Plates for metal fabrications to ISO 3574 and ISO 6317.
Ungalvanized steel sheet hot- or cold-rolled, except use cold-rolled where finished work will be exposed to view.
Hot-rolled steel sheet to ISO 4995 (commercial steel).
Cold-rolled steel sheet to ISO 4997 (commercial steel).
Cold reduced steel sheet qualities to ISO 3574 where applicable.
Bolts, nuts and washers for structural steel framing to NBN EN 1090, Grade 8.8 unless noted otherwise.
High strength bolts for structural steel accessories to conform to NBN EN 1993 and NBN EN 14399.
All bolts shall be new and not re-used.
Direct tension indicators shall meet requirements of NBN EN 14399.
Bolts, nuts and washers for metal fabrications to EN ISO 898.
Provide zinc coated fasteners for exterior use or where built into exterior walls in metal fabrications.
Anchor bolts for structural steel to NBN EN 15048, grade as specified in design documents, non-headed type unless otherwise indicated.

Mechanical fasteners and sidelap connectors for steel decking: proprietary systems such as Hilti or approved alternative, with fastening pattern and capacity based on submitted and approved diaphragm calculations.

materials.grade_or_type: As per EN 1011 / EN 1090 / EN ISO 9606-1 / EN ISO 14732
specific_rules: Welding materials for structural steel to comply with NBN EN 1090 and other listed codes; type required for materials being welded.
Welding electrodes for structural steel accessories shall conform to relevant standards listed in reference standards, Group 5 of NBN EN 1993-1-8.
Welding materials for metal fabrications to comply with EN 1011.
Qualify welders for structural steel and decking per NBN EN ISO 9606-1.
Qualification testing of welding operators and weld setters per NBN EN ISO 14732 for mechanized and automatic welding of metallic materials.
Structural welding of studs for decking to EN ISO 13918 (stud shear connectors).

Welder qualifications for decking: tests per Standard Qualification Procedure of European Welding Association or relevant standards; two specimens of each weld type to be inspected and approved before welding on structure.
Welding for stairs, ramps, handrails, and guards to EN 1011, with stainless steel welding per EN 1011-3 where applicable.

Shear stud connectors for structural steel framing to be proprietary type with minimum yield strength 350 N/mm2, minimum ultimate tensile strength 450 N/mm2, minimum 15% elongation, to BS EN ISO 13918.
Stud shear connectors for decking to be proprietary type with minimum yield strength 350 N/mm2, minimum ultimate tensile strength 450 N/mm2, minimum 15% elongation, to EN ISO 13918.
Shear connectors to be shop welded to beams and girders in composite construction using automatic end welding in accordance with manufacturer’s printed instructions.
Top surface of beams onto which studs are welded to be free from mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint, and other substances detrimental to welding; ensure flange is cleaned prior to laying decking.
Do not weld studs when ambient temperature is below 0 °C.

materials.category: Grout for Steel Baseplates and Edge Angles
specific_rules: Grout for structural steel baseplates to be non-shrink, non-metallic aggregate type, capable of developing minimum compressive strength of 35 MPa at 28 days.
Grout materials to comply with Structural General Notes and Structural Drawings for structural steel works.
Grout to be shrink-resistant where specified for submittals.
Grout shall be installed solidly between column plates and bearing surfaces in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions; trowel grouted surfaces smooth, splaying neatly to 45 degrees.

materials.category: Primers and Paints (General Steel Corrosion Protection)
materials.grade_or_type: Rust inhibitive primers and coating systems
specific_rules: Shop and touch-up primer for structural steel framing to be fabricator’s standard grey rust inhibitive primer complying with VOC limitations of authorities having jurisdiction.
Touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces in structural steel framing to be fabricator’s standard complying with VOC limitations.
Shop and touch-up primer for metal fabrications to comply with EN ISO 8503-1 preparation requirements.
Touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces in metal fabrications to comply with EN ISO 17463.
Prime painting for metal fabrications: one coat grey metal primer or approved equal, applied to minimum dry film thickness of 50 microns.
Preparation of steel prior to shop finishing for stairs and metal fabrications in accordance with coating manufacturer’s preparation requirements.
All external and exposed metal fabrications, handrails, stairs and ramps to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for a C4 environment to EN ISO 12944-2 and ISO 9223.
Steel deck units and sheet accessories to be produced from galvanized steel sheet conforming to NBN EN 10346 and NBN EN 10143, Grade of steel S350 unless indicated or agreed otherwise.
Deck units shall be free of materials such as dirt, rust, and rolling oils that are detrimental to bond of finishes.
Roof deck shall be wide rib units and shall have no stiffening ribs in top surface.
Accessory metal such as slab edge pour stops, edge strips, closure strips, sump pans to be minimum 1.6 mm thick.
Fillers, ridge and valley plates, sheet metal closures, and necessary supports at openings to be minimum 0.8 mm thick.

materials.category: Miscellaneous Steel Fabrications (Ladders, Rails, Guards, Frames)
materials.grade_or_type: Carbon steel and galvanized steel components
specific_rules: Steel ladder side rails/stiles to be manufacturer’s standard steel flat bar members with eased edges, spaced at maximum 600 mm.
Ladder rungs to be 20-50 mm rectangular steel, maximum 600 mm width between stiles.
Vertical spacing of ladder rungs to be 225-300 mm, consistent within each flight, with maximum 6 m height before intermediate landing required.
Space ladder rungs 175 mm from wall surface, measured to rung centerline.

Support each ladder at top, bottom, and intermediate points spaced not more than 1500 mm apart, using welded or bolted steel brackets to maintain minimum 175 mm clearance from wall to rung centerline.
Extend ladder rails minimum 1100 mm above top rung and return rails to wall or structure or goose-neck as required for secure access.
Provide safety cage hoops above 3 m from finished floor level where shown.
Barrier rails to be Schedule 40 mm diameter steel pipe and steel channel sections with galvanized finish.
Ledge angles, shelf angles, channels, and plates not attached to primary structural framing for support of metal decking to be galvanized.
Roof opening framing for metal fabrications to be as detailed, with prime paint or galvanized finish.

Concrete edge confinement angles to be steel angles with galvanized finish, with loose structural steel angles with integral anchor bolts and drilled/tapped angle legs for machine screw connection to forms, and anchorages at not greater than 1200 mm centers.
Downspout guards and cantilevered canopy supports to be galvanized finish steel as detailed.
Structural steel for stair stringers and framing to be rolled steel channels, stringer depth 300 mm.
End closure plates for stair stringers to be sheet steel of same thickness as risers, welded across ends.
Landings for stairs with concrete or metal treads to have same construction as treads and be supported and reinforced to achieve design load capacity.
Gratings for stairs and ramps to be bar gratings complying with NAAMM MBG 531 or MBG 532 as applicable, with open grid and minimum openings to meet local code requirements.
Stair risers to be closed and of same material and thickness as tread pans where used.

Nosing profiles for stairs to be sloped risers with rounded nosing of minimum radius, depth not more than 25 mm overhang, and nosing return flush with top of finished tread not more than 12.5 mm wide.
Treads for certain stairs to be galvanized mild steel or aluminum checker plate (Durbar or similar approved) with minimum 3 mm thickness, supported per structural engineer calculations.
Treads for other stairs to be steel bar grating, bearing bar depth 37.5 mm minimum.
Ramps to use steel bar grating with bearing bar depth 37.5 mm minimum.
Railings to be steel tubular pipe systems, with smooth finish continuous handrails and tube clamp systems for access-only configurations.
All external stair and ramp installations and associated components to be galvanized after fabrication or as required for local corrosion level and coating specification 09 97 13.
Handrails to be round pipe rails unless otherwise indicated, nominal diameter 32 mm.

Top rails of guards to be continuous round pipe or tube rails, nominal diameter 50 mm, sloped parallel to stair pitch/stringer with minimum 1100 mm height at landings and to meet local code requirements elsewhere.
Guardrail infill using vertical pickets of solid steel bar, square, size 12.5 mm square, horizontal spacing maximum 100 mm centers, welded to top and bottom rails.

Infill at pipe railings to use pipe or tube rails sloped parallel to stair pitch and height to meet local code requirements, pipe nominal diameter 50 mm, steel pipe or tube round, joints welded and ground smooth.
End and intermediate posts for handrails and guards to be same material and size as top rails, with maximum spacing 1.5 m or as indicated.
Rails and handrails to be galvanized after fabrication or pre-finished for C4 environment where external.
Fixed ladder guardrails to be 1100 mm high to EN 14122.
Fixed ladder rungs to be 20-50 mm rectangular steel, maximum 600 mm wide to EN 14122, vertical spacing 225-300 mm, maximum 6 m between landings.
Fixed ladder landings to be open grid or expanded metal with self-closing trap doors.
Fixed ladder guarding to use circular flat steel plate safety cage hoops to maximum 3 m above finished floor level.
All external handrail, stair and ramp installations and associated components to be pre-finished in factory to finish suitable for C4 environment to EN ISO 12944-2 and ISO 9223.
Intumescent coatings to be factory mixed formulation consisting of single-pack thin film for spray application.

System 1: Solvent-based product for internal steelwork (C1) off-site application comprising Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003 intumescent coating with dry film thickness to achieve required fire resistance, FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer with nominal DFT 25 microns as defined by EN ISO 12944-5, and FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer coat with nominal DFT 50 microns as defined by EN ISO 12944-5, or approved equivalent.

System 2: Solvent-based product for internal steelwork (C1) off-site application comprising Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002 ultra fast drying intumescent coating with DFT to achieve required fire resistance, FIRETEX C69 Fast Track Blast Primer with nominal DFT 25 microns as defined by EN ISO 12944-5, and FIRETEX M71V2 Sheen Finish top sealer coat with nominal DFT 50 microns as defined by EN ISO 12944-5, or approved equivalent.

Under certain circumstances it may be possible to apply FIRETEX FX2003 directly to steel blast-cleaned to minimum standard of Sa 2.5 to EN ISO 8501-1 with surface profile 50-100 microns; consult manufacturer’s technical department.
A/E of Record to adjust system dry film thickness makeup for alternate environment type classifications (C2, C3, C4, etc.).
Product certificates must document compatibility of intumescent coatings with primers, adhesives, and other coatings on substrates.
Provide table or printout for steel section versus required total DFT for each product type to satisfy specified fire rating on drawings.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Surface Preparation for Steel Prior to Painting
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Ensure that steel complies with Sa 2.5 (ISO 8501-1) at time of blasting, with initial rust grade A or B. Blast clean to specified Sa 2.5 preparation grade using abrasives of suitable type and size, free from contamination by fines, water, or oil; remove abrasive residues and all surface defects likely to be detrimental to protective painting system. Blast clean only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point. Remove all traces of blast residue and dust and avoid contamination of surfaces; require workmen to wear clean gloves when handling blast-cleaned steel.

finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: NBN EN ISO 12944-1; NBN EN ISO 12944-2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Apply corrosivity classifications per NBN EN ISO 12944-2: internal steelwork class C2 and external steelwork class C4 unless otherwise stated in project documentation. Submit corrosion protection proposals including durability ranges per NBN EN ISO 12944-1 clause 5.5, from low (L, up to 7 years) to very high (VH, more than 25 years). Ensure compatibility between corrosion protection system and intumescent paint system, and coordinate with Section 07 81 23.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Corrosion Protection - Painting of Primary Steelwork
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Provide protection by painting to all primary steelwork unless noted otherwise, in compliance with NBN EN ISO 12944. Where possible, use product from one manufacturing batch; if more than one batch is used, keep separate, allocate to distinct parts or areas of the work, and inform Engineer of Record. Use coating materials strictly according to manufacturer’s instructions. Confirm all coating materials are recommended for the particular surface and exposure conditions and are mutually compatible.

Complete all cutting, welding and drilling before galvanizing. Provide necessary vent and drain holes in approved locations and seal to approval after galvanizing. Galvanize all specified steelwork to EN ISO 1461. Design fabrications to minimize risk of distortion during galvanizing, using hot-rolled sections rather than cold-formed where possible, limiting jigging, weld size and amount, and maintaining uniform section thickness. Provide proper vent holes of correct size as part of good design for galvanizing. For large articles where distortion is a concern, consider single dipping or splicing structures where single dipping is not possible.

Apply specified shop coat of rust inhibitive primer in accordance with manufacturer’s product data. Apply shop coat within four hours of cleaning and before rust-bloom occurs. Carry out painting only when relative humidity is below 85% and steel surface temperature is at least 3 °C above dew point. During application, check thickness of each coat with wheel or comb gauge per EN ISO 2808. Finish shall not slump, flow, crack, flake, split, sag, pit, bubble, blister, float, effloresce, craze, shrink, break, wrinkle, crinkle, yellow, chalk, fade, discolor, powder, stain, bleed, or lose finish or gloss during specified service life. Finishes must be uniform in texture, color, and appearance within agreed sample limits and free from irregularities or distortion; coatings shall match agreed control samples where applicable. Paint all structural steel with shop coat except: members encased in concrete; members exposed to exterior outside controlled environment, where inorganic zinc-rich primer with minimum 60% volume solids and minimum 85% metallic zinc in film is required; contact surfaces of welded connections and areas within 50 mm of field welds; contact surfaces of slip-critical high-strength bolted connections; surfaces receiving sprayed-on or intumescent fireproofing, where heavy duty alkyd primer compatible with intumescent coating is used; and surfaces receiving field welded steel studs.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Additional Finish Requirement for External Steel Structures
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Finish on external steel structures must satisfy a “bright, light surface” in terms of relative absorptivity as per NBN EN 1991-1-5 to control thermal actions.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Metal Fabrications - Primed and Galvanized Finishes
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN ISO 8503-1; EN ISO 1461; EN ISO 12944-2; ISO 9223; EN ISO 17463
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Prime paint all steel fabrication items except where indicated otherwise. Galvanize items to be embedded in concrete or masonry. Do not prime surfaces in direct contact with concrete, where site welding is required, or items to be covered with sprayed fireproofing. Clean surfaces of rust, scale, grease, and foreign matter prior to finishing. Prime painting to be one coat grey metal primer or approved equal, applied to minimum DFT of 50 microns. Galvanize structural steel members after fabrication to EN ISO 1461 requirements. All external and exposed metal fabrications and associated components to be pre-finished in factory to finish suitable for C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012. Touch up abraded galvanized areas after fabrication using specified touch-up primer for galvanized surfaces in accordance with EN ISO 17463.

finishes_and_protection.system_type: Stairs, Ramps, Handrails and Guards - Shop Finishing
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Clean metal stair and railing surfaces of rust, scale, grease, and foreign matter before finishing. Do not prime surfaces in direct contact with concrete or where site welding is required. Apply one coat of specified grey metal shop primer to minimum DFT of 50 microns unless items are to be galvanized. Hot-dip galvanize external stair and railing components to minimum requirements of EN ISO 1461. Touch up abraded galvanized areas after fabrication with specified touch-up primer suitable for galvanized surfaces. All external handrail, stair and ramp installations and associated components are to be pre-finished in factory to a finish suitable for a C4 environment per EN ISO 12944-2:2017 and ISO 9223:2012.

finishes_and_protection.environment_class: C1 (internal steelwork) and adjustable to C2/C3/C4
finishes_and_protection.products_or_standards: EN 16623; EN 13381; EN 12944-5; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX2003; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX FX6002; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX C69; Sherwin Williams FIRETEX M71V2
finishes_and_protection.preparation_rules: Intumescent coatings to be reactive coatings for fire protection of metallic substrates complying with EN 16623 and tested per EN 13381-4. Primer, intumescent basecoat, and top sealer coat to be applied as a complete system. Primer dry film thickness to be as per manufacturer’s recommendation and EN ISO 12944-5. Intumescent basecoat dry film thickness to be as required to achieve specified fire resistance ratings for each steel section size. Top sealer coat dry film thickness to be as per manufacturer’s recommendation and EN ISO 12944-5. Steel substrates must be properly prepared, including cleaning of oil, grease, rolling compounds, incompatible primers, rust, and mill scale, and primed with an approved compatible primer fully cured before intumescent application. Under certain circumstances, FIRETEX FX2003 may be applied directly to steel blast cleaned to minimum Sa 2.5 per EN ISO 8501-1 with surface profile 50-100 microns, subject to manufacturer approval. Provide enclosure as necessary to confine spraying, protect environment, and maintain adequate ambient conditions (temperature, humidity, air quality, ventilation) during application, drying, and curing. Protect coatings from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity, and strong winds carrying contaminants during all application stages. Do not apply additional coats until previous layer has fully cured. Provide a uniform finish matching approved mockups or samples.

tolerances_and_rules: Steel used on the project is to be Execution Class 2 (EXC2) as defined by NBN EN 1090-2 unless noted otherwise on the A/E drawings.
Accurately confirm anchor bolt alignment, elevations, projections, and size prior to erection of superstructure; report inaccuracies or defects without delay.
Erect structural steel in compliance with local best practice guidance and NBN EN 1090 execution requirements.

Allow for erection loads and provide sufficient temporary bracing to maintain structure in safe condition, plumb, and in true alignment until completion of erection and installation of permanent bracing.
Set structural frames accurately to lines and elevations indicated. Align and adjust members forming part of complete frame before permanent fastening.
Clean bearing surfaces and other surfaces that will be in permanent contact before assembly; perform necessary adjustments to compensate for discrepancies in elevations and alignment.
Align, level, adjust, and plumb individual members of structure within EN 1090 tolerances. Setting out and construction tolerances shall be absolute, not additive.
Splice members only where indicated and accepted on shop drawings or where subsequently agreed with Engineer of Record.
Do not enlarge unfair holes in members by burning or use of drift pins; holes that must be enlarged shall be reamed, and burrs removed.

Do not use gas cutting torches in the field for correcting fabrication errors in structural framing unless acceptable to the Engineer of Record; finish gas-cut sections to a sheared appearance when permitted.
Do not field cut or alter structural members without approval of Engineer of Record.
After erection, prime welds, abrasions, and surfaces not shop primed, except surfaces to be in contact with concrete.
Grout solidly between column plates and bearing surfaces using non-shrink grout per manufacturer’s instructions; trowel grouted surfaces smooth and splay neatly to 45 degrees.
Steel erection must meet the requirements of the execution class specified for steelwork (EXC2).

execution_and_tolerances.element: Connection Design and Detailing - Structural Steel
tolerances_and_rules: Design and detail all connections to resist loads and reactions shown in design documents, but not less than robustness requirements per NBN EN 1991.
Include proper account of eccentricity in connection design for all connection components including welds, bolts, and connection materials.

Beam to column connections shall minimize eccentric loading on columns; unrestrained simple beam end connections shall be detailed and fabricated to minimize or eliminate end restraint, with connection parts designed considering eccentricity.
Beams must be designed for end shear reactions shown in design documents.
Bracing connections and all member connections must be designed for forces and actions shown in project documents.
Except for moment connections and bracing, provide bolted connections with high-strength bolted assemblies using bearing-type connections designed assuming threads included in shear plane.

Moment connections and bracing connections shall be slip-critical, detailed and erected using direct tension indicator washers or tension control bolted assemblies per manufacturer’s written instructions.
Members forming bracing systems or lattice girders shall be positioned such that their lines of action intersect at a point unless otherwise detailed or instructed.
All connections and details shown on shop and erection drawings must be prepared under supervision of Contractor’s Engineer in accordance with NBN EN 1993.

Contractor shall design and provide stiffener plates, doubler plates, reinforcing plates, and their connections as required to develop and transfer forces and meet connection design criteria in Contract Documents.

All forces shown on drawings are to be assumed reversible unless noted otherwise and must be checked for both directions; where no forces are shown, assume most critical combinations of member forces and directions.

For high restraint welds, use double bevels instead of single bevels where practical; detail joints to allow for weld shrinkage; for plates in more than one plane, show welding sequence on drawings and generally start welding at most restrained part of weldment progressing to least restrained.
Comply with all connection notes on drawings in conjunction with specifications.

Connection design calculations must be numbered in a logical, consistent system; resubmittals use same number with 'R' suffix and changes clouded. Alternate numbering may be mandated in BIM Execution Plan or other project documentation.

Provide sketches for each calculation showing all pertinent dimensions (pitch, gauge, edge distance, unbraced lengths, Whitmore length assumptions, etc.) with accurate and to-scale geometry. Provide sufficient sketches for full range of geometric conditions.
For repetitive connections, provide spreadsheet or computer program summary table for each specific location with standard calculations showing basis for table.
Provide drawings showing overall locations of connections keyed or referenced to each connection calculation.

Calculations may be typed, spreadsheet-based, computer program-based, or other method approved by Engineer of Record; spreadsheets must show input and results for every step and include explanatory text and sketches.
Provide calculation checks for all forces shown on drawings; all NBN EN 1993 code requirements apply; 'OK by inspection' is not permitted.

Fabricate structural steel members in accordance with all relevant EN codes including national annexes and complementary standards, plus national best practice documents for steel buildings and bridges.
Shop fabricate to greatest extent possible; fabricate for delivery sequence minimizing field handling.
Identify and record materials and components; submit details of proposed identification and recording methods.
Place identification marks where visible for checking after erection but not on faces exposed to view, subject to Architect’s approval.
Where finishing is required, complete assembly including welding before starting finishing operations; provide finished surfaces of exposed members free of markings, burrs, and other defects.
Shop connections to be welded or bolted as indicated; field connections generally to be bolted except where welded or other connection types are indicated.

Provide high-strength threaded fasteners for principal bolted connections except where unfinished bolts are indicated; use unfinished threaded fasteners only for secondary framing to primary members and for temporary bracing to facilitate erection.
Install high-strength threaded fasteners in accordance with NBN EN 14399 and NBN EN 15048, with hardened washers under element turned in tightening to facilitate verification.
Welded construction to comply with NBN EN 1090 including all inspection, testing, and acceptance requirements.
Assemble and weld built-up sections using methods that ensure true alignment of axis without warp.

Provide holes required for securing other work to structural steel framing and for passage of other work through framing members as shown on final approved shop drawings; cut, drill or punch holes perpendicular to metal surfaces; do not flame cut or enlarge holes by burning; drill holes in bearing plates and remove all burrs from drilling.
Provide header units to support tail joists at openings in floor or roof systems unless otherwise indicated.
Develop specified camber for members per drawings; where no camber is indicated, fabricate beams so that natural camber is upward after erection.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Temporary Support of Structural Steel Frame
tolerances_and_rules: The structure as shown in Contract Documents is designed to withstand design loads only when all structural elements are installed and fully connected.
Contractor is responsible for analysis of all components and assemblies for stresses and displacements due to fabrication, shipping, handling, erection, temporary conditions, and construction loads.
Analysis of temporary and construction stages shall be performed by Contractor’s Engineer.
Provide sufficient temporary support and bracing to maintain structural safety and stability during all stages until permanent bracing and full connection are completed.
Install steel deck in accordance with manufacturer’s written recommendations, approved submittals, and specified requirements.
Position metal deck units on supporting steel with accurate alignment to final position and units resting tightly on top of supporting members.
Minimum bearing of deck units on steel supporting members shall be 50 mm.
Minimum roof deck end laps shall be 50 mm.
Cuts in metal deck shall be neat and trim in appearance; cut with metal saw, drills, or cutting torch as appropriate.
Notch deck to fit around columns and similar penetrations.
Cut holes and openings that are indicated on structural drawings and approved submittals as field cuts.

Provide metal closures for openings in metal deck 1.58 mm width and over, including cover plates for panel edges and ends and where panels change direction, column closures between deck and structural columns, sheet metal collars around deck cuts for pipes and ducts, and closures, ridge and valley plates required to provide surface acceptable to roofing contractor.
No openings shall be cut in metal decking unless shown on approved submittals or specifically approved in writing by Engineer of Record.
For openings required in metal deck but not indicated on approved submittals, submit modified shop drawings and calculations for approval demonstrating compliance with all specified criteria.
Burning or weakening of metal decking material around welds is cause for rejection; deficient welds shall be repaired or entirely removed.

Anchor composite metal deck units to supporting steel by 20 mm diameter puddle welds at each end and at intermediate supports, with maximum effective average weld spacing across width of units of 300 mm on center; puddle welds not required where headed shear studs are welded through deck.
Longitudinal edges and side laps supported by steel members shall be fastened with 20 mm diameter puddle welds at maximum spacing of 300 mm on center along panel length.
Longitudinal side laps of adjacent panels without steel support shall be welded or fastened with self-tapping screws (size referenced in spec) between supports at maximum spacing of 150 mm on center.

Longitudinal edge closures shall be fastened by tack welding at maximum spacing of 600 mm on center for composite deck and 150 mm on center for non-composite deck; sheet metal screws shall not be used.
Closures and other accessories shall be adequately connected to framing steel and adjacent deck units.

For non-composite deck, puddle welds at each end and intermediate supports to 20 mm diameter with maximum effective average spacing across width of units of 200 mm on center; other spacing rules consistent with composite except where specified.
Alternative mechanical anchoring systems for metal deck such as Hilti fasteners may be used based on submitted and approved diaphragm calculations.

Shear studs for composite action to be welded through deck to primary steel members; top surfaces of beams must be clean of mill scale, rust, grease, oil, paint, and other deleterious substances before stud welding; do not weld studs when ambient temperature is below 0 °C.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Fabrications - General Fabrication and Tolerances
tolerances_and_rules: Form metal fabrications from materials of size, thickness, and shapes indicated, but not less than needed to meet performance requirements.
Work to dimensions indicated or accepted on shop drawings using proven fabrication and support details; use materials specified for each component.
Form exposed work true to line and level with accurate angles, surfaces, and straight sharp edges.
Shear and punch metals cleanly and accurately; remove burrs.
Ease exposed edges to approximately 1 mm radius unless otherwise indicated; form bent-metal corners to smallest possible radius without grain separation or impairment.
Remove sharp or rough areas on exposed traffic surfaces.
Weld corners and seams continuously to comply with EN 1011 recommendations.

Form exposed connections with hairline joints, flush and smooth, using concealed fasteners wherever possible; exposed fasteners to be Phillips flat-head (countersunk) screws or bolts where not otherwise indicated; locate joints where least conspicuous.
Provide anchorage devices of type indicated and coordinate with supporting structure; fabricate and space anchoring devices to provide adequate support.
Clearly mark shop-assembled and disassembled units for reassembly and coordinated installation.
Cut, reinforce, drill, and tap miscellaneous metal work as required to receive finish hardware, screws, and similar items.
Fabricate joints exposed to weather to exclude water or provide weep holes where water may accumulate.
Supply all components required for anchorage of fabrications; fabricate anchors and related components of same material and finish as fabrication unless otherwise noted.

If fabrications are to be galvanized, design work to avoid distortion risk, favoring hot-rolled sections, minimizing welding heat input, balancing welding procedures, and maintaining uniform section thickness.
Where distortion of large galvanized articles is a concern, consider single dipping or splicing structures to allow single dipping.

Fabrication tolerances: maximum squareness deviation 3 mm in diagonal measurements; maximum offset between faces 2 mm; maximum misalignment of adjacent members 2 mm; maximum bow 3 mm in 1200 mm; maximum deviation from plane 2 mm in 1200 mm.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Metal Stairs and Ramps - Structural and Installation Requirements
tolerances_and_rules: Design and fabricate stair assemblies and ramps including landing platforms, supports, railings, and guards, accurately for anchorage to each other and to building structure.
Provide stairs and railings complying with most stringent requirements of European and local regulations; where Contract Documents exceed code, comply with Contract Documents.
Stair clear widths, riser and going dimensions, and pitch angle must meet local code requirements.
Design stair assemblies to support uniform live load of 500 kg/m² and concentrated load of 150 kg on area of 2580 mm², with deflection of stringer or landing framing not exceeding 1/360 of span.

Handrails and railing systems must be engineered to withstand uniform load of 1.0 kN/m on top rail applied in any direction and concentrated load of 0.5 kN at any point on top rail without needing to combine these loads.
Guardrail infill areas must withstand horizontal uniform load of 1.0 kN/m² and point load of 0.5 kN without concurrent combination with top rail loads.
At exit stairwells, provide stair towers designed for stacking to building height as self-supporting structures.
Metal jointing and finish quality to be 'commercial' for exposed work: joints as inconspicuous as possible; underside of stair without soffit is considered exposed.

Welded joints on back side to be intermittent with body putty and sanded smooth; welds exposed to view to be ground smooth and flush; mechanical joints to be butted tight, flush, and hairline; exposed bolts to be countersunk flat or oval head with no exposed nuts; exposed edges and corners to be eased to small uniform radius.
Metal surfaces to be painted or galvanized to be sanded or ground smooth suitable for satin or matte finish.
For stairs and ramps with open grating, fabricate steps, landings, and ramps with bar grating tread and landing surfaces supported and reinforced to achieve design load capacity.
At electrical platforms, fabricate stairs and landings with bolted connections allowing removal and replacement for equipment maintenance.
Bridge-style roof 'stepovers' to be bigfoot-mounted and designed for height and wind loads to comply with EN 14122 requirements.

execution_and_tolerances.element: Handrails, Guards, Fixed Ladders - Installation and Tolerances
tolerances_and_rules: Fabricate pipe handrails and railing systems to meet specified design, dimensions, detail, finish, and member sizes, including wall thickness of pipe, post spacing, and anchorage sufficient for structural loads.
Interconnect railing and handrail members by butt welding or using internal connectors unless indicated otherwise.

At tee and cross intersections, mitre ends of intersecting members to fit contour of pipe joined and weld all around; where site welding is restricted, use concealed couplings with rivet fixings subject to A/E review.
Form changes in direction of handrails and rails using prefabricated flush elbow fittings, radius bends per indicated radii, flush radius bends, or bending, as applicable to each change.
Form simple and compound curves by bending pipe in jigs to produce uniform curvature, maintaining cylindrical cross section without buckling, twisting, cracking, or deforming exposed surfaces.
Provide wall returns at ends of wall-mounted handrails unless otherwise indicated, extending handrails beyond first/last nosing line per local code.
Close exposed ends of pipe with 2 mm thick steel plate welded in place or with prefabricated fittings.
Locate drain and vent holes in pipes in inconspicuous locations and plug all holes before delivery to site.
Provide brackets, flanges, fittings, and anchors for interconnection of pipe components and attachment of systems to other work, including inserts and anchorage devices for concrete or masonry.
Install components plumb and level, accurately fitted, and free from distortion or defects.
Provide anchors, plates, angles, hangers, and struts needed for connecting stairs to structure.
Allow for erection loads and provide sufficient temporary bracing to maintain true alignment until permanent attachments are installed.
Provide welded site joints where specifically indicated; perform site welding per EN 1011. Other site joints may be welded or bolted provided required jointing quality levels are met.
Mechanically fastened joints must be butted tight, flush, and hairline, with welds ground smooth and flush.
Obtain approval prior to site cutting or unplanned adjustments.
After erection, prime weld abrasions and unprimed or ungalvanized surfaces except those in direct contact with concrete.

For steel pipe railings and handrails, adjust systems before anchoring to achieve matching alignment at abutting joints; space posts as indicated or as required by design loads; plumb posts in each direction.
Anchor posts to steel by welding directly to supporting steel members.
Anchor handrail ends into concrete and masonry with steel round flanges welded to rail ends and drilled-in expansion anchors.
Secure handrails to walls with brackets and end fittings, providing minimum 50 mm clearance from wall face to inside face of handrail; locate brackets as indicated or as necessary to support loads.
Use wall brackets with flanges tapped for concealed anchorage to threaded hanger bolts.

For concrete and solid masonry, use drilled-in expansion anchors for handrail brackets; for steel-framed gypsum board assemblies, fasten brackets to steel framing or concealed anchors using self-tapping screws of adequate size and type.

Fixed ladders: install rails, rungs, guards, and landings per manufacturer’s standard and EN 14122 requirements with specified spacings and heights, including self-closing trap doors at landings and safety cage hoops positioned appropriately.
Maximum variation from plumb for handrail and guard installations is 6 mm; maximum offset from true alignment is 6 mm.
Install intumescent coatings only after verifying steel members have been properly prepared and primed with compatible primer or that existing shop primer is approved and in satisfactory condition.
Comply with intumescent coating manufacturer’s written instructions for mixing, application procedures, and equipment.
Provide enclosures as required to confine spraying, protect environment, and maintain ambient conditions (temperature, humidity, air quality, and ventilation) during application.
Clean substrates to remove oil, grease, rolling compounds, incompatible primers, rust, and mill scale before priming or coating.
Prime substrates with approved compatible primer unless an adequate compatible shop primer is present and fully cured.
Protect intumescent coatings from rain, direct sunlight, high humidity, and strong winds with dust or sand during application, drying, and curing unless test evidence allows otherwise.
Do not apply additional coats of intumescent coating until previous layer has fully cured as per manufacturer.
Apply primer to specified dry film thickness per manufacturer and EN ISO 12944-5.
Apply intumescent basecoat to dry film thickness needed to achieve specified fire resistance ratings for each member.
Apply top sealer coat to specified dry film thickness per manufacturer and EN ISO 12944-5.
Provide uniform final appearance matching approved mockups or control samples.

qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide shop drawings of individual structural steel shipping pieces to be fabricated in the shop, prepared and checked prior to issue by a suitably qualified professional Structural Engineer. Provide erection drawings and method statements showing location and connections of individual shipping pieces, and temporary works drawings and method statements prepared by erector showing sequence of erection, locations of bracing and temporary supports, and description of bolting, welding, and lifting operations.

Submit calculations for all connection designs before preparation of shop drawings. Calculations must be numbered logically and consistently, with resubmittals using same number plus 'R' suffix and changes clouded. Provide sketches showing geometry and relevant dimensions for each calculation, including assumptions for Whitmore lengths and other force distributions. Provide summary tables and supporting standard calculations for repetitive connection types. Supply drawings keyed to each connection calculation. Calculations must be typed or prepared by spreadsheet or computer program with all inputs and results clearly shown, including explanatory text and sketches. 'OK by inspection' is not permitted; provide full checks for all forces shown on drawings in accordance with NBN EN 1993.

Submit a Quality Plan for the execution of structural steel works in accordance with recommendations of NBN EN 1090 at the earliest possible time after appointment. Undertake fabrication and erection work in accordance with this Quality Plan.

Provide manufacturer’s Mill Certificates certifying that all structural steel products meet or exceed specified requirements. Submit certification of welders employed on structural steel work verifying qualification in line with NBN EN ISO 9606-1 within previous 12 months. Provide confirmation of membership of a national Constructional Steelwork Association or other relevant organisation. Provide confirmation of CE Marking Accreditation for execution class relevant to the project. Include specific submittals for shrink resistant grout, welding electrodes for each type, shear studs, and direct tension indicators.

Contractor shall verify in writing in a submittal that structural steel contains 70 percent recycled content (pre-consumer and post-consumer). Copy of submittal must be sent concurrently to EXE and DC Sustainability for tracking. If compliance is not possible due to availability, schedule, or cost, contractor must submit a written request for exception to Engineer of Record at time of submittal, also copied to EXE and DC Sustainability.

At least 14 days before beginning structural steel erection, contractor shall conduct a pre-construction conference to review quality control, construction requirements, submittals, coordination, and schedules. Attendance required from construction manager, contractor’s site engineer, special inspection and testing agency, structural steel detailer, fabricator, erector, Engineer of Record, and architect if required. Contractor must notify external parties at least 7 days in advance. Minutes must be recorded, typed, printed, and distributed within 5 days, with copies to Owner’s representative, architect, and Engineer of Record. Similarly, at least 20 working days prior to steel erection, contractor shall hold a pre-erection conference with general contractor, steel erector/fabricator, erector’s surveyor, roof deck contractor, testing and inspection agencies, design professionals, owner, and precast or cladding contractor as appropriate. Minutes must include detailed erection procedure, schedule of surveys and sign-offs, surveying program, and submission schedule. Responsibility for organizing these conferences lies solely with contractor, and failure is deemed poor attention to specified requirements.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Connection Design and Detailing Workshop - Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: At least 20 working days before starting connection design and detailing, fabricator shall hold a workshop to verify connection design assumptions, procedures, and shop drawing preparation and submittal procedures. Contractor shall prepare agenda and require attendance from general contractor, fabricator, detailer, connection engineer, Engineer of Record, and erector. Fabricator shall distribute meeting minutes to all parties within 5 working days. Workshop is not a substitute for formal submittals and approvals, and any comments by A/E of Record are non-binding relative to formal reviews.

An independent testing agency shall perform field quality control tests for structural steel as specified in Section 01 40 00. Provide testing and verification of all field high-strength bolted connections and visual inspection of all field-welded connections. Reinspection is required for all failed tests at no cost or time delay to owner.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Steel Decking Shop Drawings and Calculations
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit shop drawings for steel decking including deck type, identification mark, gauge, finish, location, openings, dimensions, placement sequence, anchorage details, lap details, accessories, and welding data, including power requirements and type of electrodes. Welding symbols shall conform to relevant European Welding Association standards. Indicate locations of unframed openings, including those to be cut after topping and details of deck closures and deck reinforcement, and type and location of inserts. Provide product data with deck profile characteristics, dimensions, structural properties, and finishes. Provide design calculations signed and sealed by a Professional Engineer specializing in structural engineering covering section properties for each deck type and gauge and slab edge and closure strips. Shop drawings will not be reviewed without accompanying calculations; review does not relieve originator or supervising engineer of responsibility.

Maintain records of welder qualification data available for examination. Qualify welders by tests as prescribed in Standard Qualification Procedure of the European Welding Association or relevant standards. Unless stricter standards or regulations apply, each welder shall prepare two specimens of each type of weld required; specimens to be inspected, tested, and approved by Inspection and Testing Agency before welding on structure.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Decking Delivery, Storage, and Handling Controls
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: For steel decking, cut plastic wrap to encourage ventilation and store deck on dry wood sleepers sloped for positive drainage. Protect deck from corrosion, deformation, and other damage during delivery, storage, and handling with waterproof covering and ventilation to avoid condensation.

Submit shop drawings for metal fabrications indicating profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, size and type of fasteners, and accessories. Include erection drawings, elevations, and details as applicable. Indicate welded connections using standard ISO 2553 welding symbols and show net weld lengths.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Welding Qualifications - Metal Fabrications and Stairs
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit welders' certificates documenting suitable qualification within previous 12 months for welders employed on metal fabrication and stair work. Qualify welding processes and welding operators in accordance with EN 1011 and EN 1011-3 for stainless steel where applicable.

Fabricator of metal fabrications must be experienced in producing similar fabrications with sufficient capacity to avoid delays. Fabricators of steel stairs must have record of successful in-service performance for similar projects. Structural design to be under direct supervision of Professional Engineer experienced in design of the work and licensed in the project state or local jurisdiction.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Sequencing and Shop Assembly - Metal Fabrications
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Preassemble metal fabrications in shop to greatest extent possible to minimize field splicing and assembly. Disassemble units only as necessary for shipping and handling limitations. Clearly mark fabricated units for reassembly and coordinated installation. Schedule production and site delivery to avoid delays to other work and to prevent site congestion with stored materials.

Submit shop drawings for stairs and railings indicating profiles, sizes, connection attachments, reinforcing, anchorage, size and type of fasteners, and accessories. Indicate welded connections using standard welding symbols with net weld lengths. Include design engineer’s signature on each sheet of stair and railing shop drawings.

Fabricator of stairs must be experienced in producing steel stairs similar to those indicated for the project with record of successful performance. Structural designer must be a Professional Engineer experienced in stair and railing design and licensed in locality. Verify suitable qualifications of welders employed on stair and railing work within previous 12 months.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Fire Protection Product Data and Test Evidence
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Submit product data sheet/specification for each intumescent coating system. For each system, provide test results from independent fire test laboratory based on EN 13381-4 procedures, along with assessment of test results used to calculate optimum thickness for full range of section sizes covered in test program. Assessment must be issued through organization subscribing to Passive Fire Protection Federation guide to undertaking assessments in lieu of fire tests. Provide product certificates from manufacturer documenting compatibility of intumescent coatings with adhesives, primers, and other surface coatings. Provide table or printout for each product type showing steel section versus required dry film thickness to meet specified fire rating on drawings.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Fire Protection Samples and Installer Qualifications
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Provide samples of each exposed intumescent product for each color and texture, 200 mm square. Installer must submit qualification data demonstrating capabilities and experience on comparable projects including project location, scope of work, project type, contract value, completion date, architect contact, and owner contact. Installer must be certified, licensed, or otherwise qualified by intumescent coating manufacturer and trained by manufacturer’s direct employees. Manufacturer must have local technical employees available and provide technical representative on site at start of installation and as requested.

At least 14 days before beginning intumescent fireproofing application, contractor shall conduct a meeting to review quality control and construction requirements for intumescent coatings and determine procedures to achieve proper installation. Review submittal requirements, coordination, material availability, schedule, and procedures for inspections, testing, certifications, and reporting. Require attendance from construction manager, contractor’s site engineer, special inspection and testing agency, fireproofing applicator, Engineer of Record, and architect if required. Minutes must be recorded, typed and distributed to all parties within 5 days, with copies to owner’s representative, architect, and A/E of Record. Notify external parties at least 7 days prior to conference.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Intumescent Coating Delivery, Storage, and Handling
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: Deliver intumescent coatings in original unopened packages with intact labels. Apply coatings before expiration date specified on packaging; remove and properly discard expired product per regulations. Store coatings protected from direct sunlight and at manufacturer-specified temperatures; prevent freezing. Identify and remove from site any materials damaged by improper storage.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Field Quality Control - Intumescent Fire Protection
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: An independent testing agency shall perform field quality control tests of intumescent coatings as specified in Section 01 40 00. Inspection scope includes checking surface preparation standards (usually EN ISO 8501-1), surface profile per EN ISO 8503-2, dust and contamination per visual assessment or EN ISO 8502-3, environmental conditions (air temperature, substrate temperature, humidity, dew point) versus specification or manufacturer data during application, recording batch numbers, dates and times of application, compliance with overcoating intervals, wet film thickness checks, and dry film thickness surveys at primer, after intumescent basecoat, and upon completion. DFT measurement sampling includes specified numbers of readings per meter on webs and flanges of I and T sections, and faces of hollow sections and angles; for members under 2 m, three sets of readings at ends and center. Acceptance criteria: average DFT on each element must be greater or equal to specified nominal value; average DFT on any face must not be less than 80% of nominal; values below 80% are acceptable only if isolated and not more than 10% of readings per member, and all readings must be at least 50% of nominal. Additional readings must be taken around any low reading below 80% to determine if isolated; areas of under-thickness must be brought up to required thickness before proceeding. Average DFT on any face should not exceed manufacturer’s recommended maximum for that member shape and orientation.

Before installation of structural steel, metal fabrications, stairs, and railings, verify that site and supporting conditions prepared by others are acceptable and ready to receive work; report any defects to design professionals. Commencement of work implies acceptance of preparatory work by others. Supply setting templates to appropriate parties for steel items requiring casting into concrete or embedding in masonry. Clean and strip primed steel items to bare metal where site welding is required.

qa_qc_and_submittals.requirement_type: Holding Down Bolt and Anchor Rod Survey - Structural Steel
qa_qc_and_submittals.description: At least 20 working days before starting structural steel erection, contractor shall survey existing location, alignment, and elevation of anchor rods embedded in foundation works by others. Immediately notify design professionals of discrepancies between contract documents and as-built conditions. Do not start steel erection until required corrective measures have been performed.

An independent testing agency shall perform site quality control tests for steel decking. All field-welded decking connections must be visually inspected to verify conformance with specified welding patterns and quality.
